title: Reasoning and Tool-use Compete in Agentic RL:From Quantifying Interference to Disentangled Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2602.00994v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Agentic Reinforcement Learning (ARL) trains large language models to interleave reasoning with external tool execution to solve complex tasks. Most existing ARL methods train a single set of parameters to support both reasoning and tool-use behaviors, implicitly assuming that joint training leads to improved overall agent performance. Despite its widespread adoption, this assumption has rarely been examined empirically. In this paper, we systematically examine this assumption by introducing Capability Effect Attribution (CEA), which provides quantitative evidence of interference between reasoning and tool-use behaviors. Through an in-depth analysis, we show that these two capabilities often induce misaligned gradient directions, leading to training interference that undermines the effectiveness of joint optimization and challenges the prevailing ARL paradigm. translated_title: 智能体强化学习中推理与工具使用的相互竞争：从干扰量化到解耦调优
translated_abstract: 智能体强化学习（ARL）训练大语言模型将推理与外部工具执行交替进行，以解决复杂任务。现有的大多数ARL方法使用单一参数集来同时支持推理和工具使用行为，隐含地假设联合训练能够提升智能体的整体性能。尽管这一假设被广泛采用，却很少经过实证检验。本文通过引入能力效应归因（CEA）系统地检验了这一假设，为推理与工具使用行为之间的干扰提供了量化证据。深入分析表明，这两种能力常常导致梯度方向不一致，引发训练干扰，从而削弱联合优化的有效性，并对当前主流的ARL范式提出挑战。为解决这一问题，我们提出了动作-推理解耦调优（DART）方法。
tldr: 该论文通过能力效应归因（CEA）量化揭示了智能体强化学习中推理与工具使用能力因梯度方向不一致而产生的训练干扰，并提出动作-推理解耦调优（DART）方法来克服联合训练的干扰问题。
en_tdlr: This paper quantitatively reveals training interference between reasoning and tool-use capabilities in agentic RL via Capability Effect Attribution (CEA), attributing it to misaligned gradient directions, and proposes Disentangled Action–Reasoning Tuning (DART) to address it.
